summary: Zesho Machida worked in Buddhist studies. Machida held posts at Minobusan Okunoin Shishinkaku (attested 1990) and Minobusan University (attested 1996–2001).

Zev Handel specializes in linguistics, Sinology, and Tibetology. He studied at Harvard College (1988) and the University of California, Berkeley (1992, 1998), later becoming a professor at the University of Washington around 1999.
Zhao Luo works in Buddhist studies, history, archaeology, and Tibetology. He studied under Sen Wang and held a post as a scholar at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (attested 2014).
Zhaohua Yang is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. Yang held posts at Stanford University (attested 2007) and Columbia University (attested 2018).

Zhe Ji is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He earned a Ph.D. in sociology from the School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences in 2007 and served as an Associate Professor at INALCO (attested 2011–2017).
Zhen Liu specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Sinology. Liu earned master's degrees from the University of Munich in 2005 and Lanzhou University in 2009.
Zhengyan Fan works in Buddhist studies and Indology. Fan is attested in 2026 as a PhD researcher and faculty member at Ghent University.
Zhenhua (1922–2021) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Tianning Buddhist College in 1947 and under Yinshun in 1952. Zhenhua served as manager at Fuyan Buddhist Institute (attested 1992).

Zhihua Yao is a scholar in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Boston University (~1997–2002) under Malcolm David Eckel, later holding posts at the University of Hong Kong (~2003–2005) and The Chinese University of Hong Kong (~2005).

Zhiru Ng specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. Ng earned an MA under Luis Oscar Gómez at the University of Michigan and a PhD under Robert M. Gimello at the University of Arizona.

Zhiru Shi (born 1964) works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. Shi studied at the University of Michigan (MA 1993) and the University of Arizona (PhD), later holding posts at Pomona College (attested 2007–2014) and Fo Guang University (attested 2026).

Zhiyi Yang (born 1979) is a Sinologist. Educated at Peking University, Princeton University (PhD under Martin Kern), and the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg, Yang held posts at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg and Goethe University Frankfurt (attested 2015).

Zhonghui Cui works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and history and archaeology. Cui earned an MA from SOAS University of London and a PhD from the University of Hong Kong, where Cui held an academic post attested in 2013.
Zhongpei Zhang (1934–2017) worked in history, archaeology, and Sinology. He studied under Su Bai (~1952–1956) and served as director at the Palace Museum from around 1987 to 1991.

Zhongxin Jiang (1942–2002) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Peking University under Xianlin Ji (~1962–1968), later working at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (~1978–2002), Peking University, and Soka University (attested 1999).
Zhuan Dao (1871–1943) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Tongzhi. He founded Poo Thor Jee in 1911 and Kong Meng San Phor Kark See Monastery in 1920.
Zijie Li works in Buddhist studies. Li studied at Komazawa University and held a post at the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science as a DC research fellow, both attested in 2015.

Zoltán Gombocz (1877–1935) was a scholar in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Berzsenyi Dániel Evangélikus Gimnázium until 1895 and at Eötvös Loránd University from 1895 to 1900.

Zong Rinpoche (1905–1984) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure who studied at Ganden Shartse Monastery, Gyuto Monastery, and under Trijang Rinpoche. He served as Abbot of Ganden Shartse Monastery (1937–1946) and Rektor at CIHTS (1967–1971).

Zongsan Mou (1909–1995) was a philosopher and Sinologist who studied at Peking University under Shili Xiong. He held posts at West China Union, NTU, NTNU, Tunghai, HKU, CUHK, and the New Asia Institute of Advanced Chinese Studies.
